results.title: Cottage cheese pie recipe: precise cooling requirements for perfect slice structural stability
results.description: The structure of this cottage cheese pie relies on a fundamental contrast between a crumbly, short-crust base and a dense, custard-like filling. The defining characteristic of the pastry is its tenderness, which is achieved through the specific state of the fat and the method of incorporation. The Role of Temperature and Texture The decisive action in this recipe is the use of frozen butter (125g) grated directly into a mixture of 1 cup of wheat flour, 2 tablespoons of sugar, 1 teaspoon of baking powder, and a pinch of salt. By keeping the butter frozen and rubbing it quickly by hand into the dry ingredients, the baker prevents the fat from emulsifying with the flour. This creates a "rubbed-in" texture-a coarse crumb-rather than a cohesive dough. This specific state ensures that the pastry remains tender and flaky rather than tough or bread-like after it hits the 180°C oven. Filling Stability and Assembly While the crust provides the architecture, the filling is governed by the binding properties of 2 egg yolks. The mixture of 350g of cottage cheese, 1.2 cups of sugar, and 1.2 teaspoons of vanilla extract must be worked with a fork until homogeneous. The yolks act as the primary stabilizer, transforming the cottage cheese into a smooth mass that can support the weight of the topping without collapsing.
